questionText: A company uses a purchased AI assistant, unchanged, under its own authority. What is its role?
explanation: Whoever uses someone else's AI system under their own authority in a professional context is a deployer (Art. 3(4)).

questionText: A distributor puts its own brand on someone else's high-risk system and sells it. What follows?

answerOptions.text: It stays a distributor as long as it changes no code
It counts as the provider of this system under Art. 25

explanation: Whoever puts their name or trademark on a high-risk system counts as its provider under Art. 25(1), with the obligations under Art. 16.

questionText: A provider with no EU establishment supplies AI output that a company in Germany uses. Does the AI Act apply to it?

answerOptions.text: Yes, because the output is used in the EU (Art. 2(1)(c))
No, only the place of establishment counts
Only if its servers are in the EU

explanation: Art. 2(1)(c) covers providers and deployers outside the EU when the system's output is used in the Union.

questionText: Who is excluded from the scope of the AI Act?

answerOptions.text: Small companies with fewer than ten staff
Natural persons using AI purely for personal, non-professional purposes
Companies that only use open-source models

explanation: Art. 2(10) excludes purely personal use by natural persons. There is no SME exemption from the scope.

questionText: Since when has Art. 4 (AI literacy) applied?
explanation: Under Art. 113(a), Art. 4 has applied since 2 February 2025. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 changed its content, not this date.

questionText: From when do the high-risk rules for stand-alone systems under Annex III apply?
explanation: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026, sets 2 December 2027 for Annex III and 2 August 2028 for product-embedded systems under Annex I.

questionText: From when must a website chatbot be recognisable as AI under Art. 50(1)?

answerOptions.text: From 2 August 2026, at the latest at the first interaction
Only if it processes personal data

explanation: Art. 50 applies from 2 August 2026. The notice must be clear and come at the latest at the first interaction (Art. 50(5)).

questionText: A tool analyses and ranks incoming applications. What risk class is this use?
explanation: Annex III point 4(a) covers AI for recruitment or selection, in particular analysing and filtering applications.

questionText: A company wants to use AI to infer employees' emotions in video calls. Is that allowed?

answerOptions.text: No, prohibited under Art. 5(1)(f), except for medical or safety reasons
Yes, from 2 December 2027 as a high-risk system

explanation: Emotion recognition in the workplace has been prohibited since 2 February 2025. Consent or works council approval does not cure it.

questionText: What risk class is a conventional email spam filter?
explanation: No prohibition, no annex, no Art. 50 case: minimal risk. Art. 4 still applies.

questionText: An Annex III system only performs a preparatory task but profiles people in doing so. Does the Art. 6(3) exception apply?

answerOptions.text: Yes, preparatory tasks are always exempt
No, an Annex III system that profiles people is always high-risk
Yes, if a human decides at the end

explanation: Art. 6(3), third subparagraph: an Annex III system is always high-risk if it profiles natural persons.

questionText: An HR chatbot holds pre-interviews and pre-sorts applicants. What applies?

answerOptions.text: Only Art. 50, because it is a chatbot
High-risk under Annex III point 4 plus the AI notice under Art. 50(1)
Minimal risk, as long as a human decides

explanation: The purpose sets the class; direct interaction adds the notice. Art. 50 applies to high-risk systems too.

questionText: For how long, at minimum, do deployers keep automatically generated logs of a high-risk system under their control?

answerOptions.text: Six months, unless other law provides otherwise
Not at all; that is the provider's job

explanation: Art. 26(6) requires at least six months. Ten years applies to the provider's technical documentation (Art. 18).

questionText: A private machine builder uses a CV screening tool (Annex III point 4). Does it need a fundamental rights impact assessment under Art. 27?

answerOptions.text: Yes, every high-risk system needs one
No, Art. 27 covers public bodies, private providers of public services and Annex III point 5(b) and (c)
No, because Art. 27 only applies from 2030

explanation: Employment AI under Annex III point 4 is not among the Art. 27 addressees. The Art. 26 obligations remain.

questionText: An agency publishes a deceptively real AI video of a real person. Who must disclose the deepfake?

answerOptions.text: The agency, as deployer, under Art. 50(4)
Only the provider of the video tool

explanation: Disclosure on publication falls to the deployer (Art. 50(4)). The provider marks its output machine-readably (para. 2).

questionText: What does Art. 50(2) require of providers of generative systems?

answerOptions.text: A visible footnote under every text

explanation: Providers mark generated audio, image, video and text content in a machine-readable way that is, as far as technically feasible, effective, interoperable, robust and reliable.

questionText: What is the maximum fine for prohibited practices under Art. 99(3)?

answerOptions.text: EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover

explanation: Undertakings face the higher of the two values, SMEs the lower under Art. 99(6).

questionText: An SME with EUR 20 million annual turnover uses a prohibited practice. What is the maximum fine?
explanation: 7% of EUR 20 million is EUR 1.4 million. For SMEs the lower value applies (Art. 99(6)).

questionText: Which authority does the KI-MIG, in force since 29 July 2026, make the single point of contact and default market surveillance authority?
explanation: The BNetzA is market surveillance authority, single point of contact and complaints body wherever no sectoral authority is competent.

questionText: You build a large provider's language model into your software via an API. Who carries the Art. 53 obligations?

answerOptions.text: You, because you use the model
The model provider; among other things it must give you the Annex XII information

explanation: Art. 53 binds the provider of the GPAI model and has applied since 2 August 2025. For your own system you are provider or deployer with your own obligations.
